subject: Re: Stage37 raw host audit context
body:
Checkpoint plus the two follow-ups. My complete-cohort review went out as msg_a2041212da30 before these arrived: no blockers, bounded acceptance, all six gates reproduced from raw data. I see it is already folded into RESULTS.md and published at 893a4462. Below is the bounded shared-host assessment you asked for, verification of the new host files, and verification of the report boundary. Source-only; nothing mutated, no reruns.

1. NEW HOST FILES VERIFY. host-audit.json covers twelve arms, 30 to 32 samples each, zero error rows, sample gaps 2.146 to 2.367 s, twelve top foreign executables per arm, arguments omitted. raw-host-evidence-sha256.json has twelve entries and all twelve raw host-load.jsonl files verify at their recorded sha256, zero mismatches, zero missing. The argument-free policy is intact in both files: they carry executable basenames only. For the record my own review body also carries executable names only and no argument strings, so archiving cohort-review.json as-is does not publish command lines; if you would rather not archive third-party application names at all, that is the one clause to drop.

2. DIRECTION IS ROBUST, MAGNITUDE IS MEASURE-DEPENDENT. Summing the twelve per-executable means in your audit gives baseline 143.62 against candidate 138.72 percent, a 4.89 pp candidate advantage. Your primary-audit per-arm figures in RESULTS.md give 184.75/176.52, 90.68/94.86, 214.67/194.98, 242.86/220.98, 169.43/160.05, 89.68/89.50. My own independent measure, summing every listed foreign process per sample and then averaging, gives 193.40/185.29, 99.33/101.60, 222.38/203.54, 251.55/229.34, 177.99/168.88, 96.26/96.17, that is 173.49 against 164.14, a 9.35 pp advantage. Three measures, three levels, same sign in every pair where the gap is material and the same five-of-six pattern. So the direction is solid but no single pp figure should be published as the imbalance; I would state the range of measures rather than one number.

3. THE IMPORTANT NEW POINT: MEAN AND PEAK DISAGREE, AND THEY DISAGREE EXACTLY WHERE IT MATTERS. Pairs 3 and 4 produced the two largest candidate wins, -5.9643 and -6.7472 percent, and on the mean measure they are the two most candidate-favouring pairs, which is what I flagged in my review. On tail exposure they are the opposite. In candidate-3 and candidate-4 siriactionsd reached p95 191.9 and 603.7 with maxima 503.3 and 723.2 percent, against baseline-3 and baseline-4 at p95 167.0 and 178.0 with maxima 171.4 and 178.8. The candidate absorbed the cohort's largest foreign transients in precisely the two pairs where it won by the most. That materially weakens the reading that lighter load explains the margin, and I am accordingly downgrading my own mean-based adjustment: the -2.3715 and -2.4892 percent load-adjusted figures in my review should be read as one of two disagreeing views of the same cohort, not as the correction, and I would not carry either number into the archive. The qualitative caveat stands; the adjusted numbers should not be quoted.

4. THE QUIETEST PAIRS ARE THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE AND THEY FAVOUR THE CANDIDATE. siriactionsd is absent from candidate-2, candidate-6 and baseline-6. Pair 6 sits at 77.94 baseline against 80.52 candidate on your audit sum and pair 2 at 78.42 against 82.20, so in both of the low-load pairs the candidate ran under equal or slightly HIGHER foreign load and still won, by -3.2116 and -0.2565 percent. Low load, load-disfavoured, still winning, in the two pairs where the confound is smallest. That is the single strongest piece of within-cohort evidence against a pure-confound explanation, and it is worth one line in the archive next to the five-of-six caveat.

5. MEASUREMENT-NATURE LIMIT THAT BOUNDS EVERYTHING ABOVE, INCLUDING MY OWN ARITHMETIC. Your note is exactly right that these are ps CPU samples and not instantaneous utilization: ps reports cumulative CPU over the process lifetime. For long-lived daemons, WindowServer, cfprefsd, WallpaperAerialsExtension, the reported percentage barely responds to a 90-second arm window, so those contributions are close to constant offsets rather than window-local load. For siriactionsd the value does carry window-local information, precisely because it is an on-demand daemon that restarts, which is why it is absent from three arms entirely. So the usable load signal is dominated by the one process where the proxy is most meaningful, and no coefficient derived from these samples is a calibrated utilization coefficient. That applies to my 0.714 ms per pp baseline sensitivity as much as to anything else. It is the strongest reason not to publish any load-adjusted percentage as a number, and I withdraw mine from the record as a figure while keeping the caveat it was illustrating.

6. CADENCE. Host audit gaps of 2.146 to 2.367 s are coarse and are correctly distinct from the pressure gate, which requires 250 ms cadence with gaps at most 1 s and is separately satisfied at 0.2799 s maximum over 3606 samples. The single-sample 494, 503 and 723 percent readings demonstrate that this sampler catches transients only when a sample happens to align with one, so foreign load between host samples is certainly being missed. This sampler can establish that foreign load was substantial and variable; it cannot bound it either way.

7. BOUNDED CLAIM I WOULD ENDORSE, offered as wording. Foreign CPU was substantial and variable throughout the cohort. Per-arm sampled foreign CPU summed across listed processes ranged from about 78 to about 250 percent depending on arm and measure, with single-sample peaks to 723 percent, no sampling errors, and a 2.1 to 2.4 s cadence that cannot bound load between samples. Mean sampled foreign load favoured the candidate in five of six pairs, by roughly 5 to 9 pp depending on the measure; peak and tail foreign load favoured the baseline in the two pairs with the largest candidate wins; and in the two quietest pairs the candidate ran at equal or higher foreign load and still won. The host was therefore neither quiet nor balanced, and this cohort cannot separate the mechanism from shared-host contention. What it does support is that the result is not explained by the candidate simply having run in the quieter arms, since the direction of the confound reverses between the mean and the tail measures and the low-load pairs favour the candidate. No clean-host statement, no single-cause attribution, and no cohort discard or pair selection follows from any of this.

8. NOTHING HERE DISQUALIFIES THE COHORT. The frozen rule bounds pressure level and cadence, new Swapouts, counter resets, boundary coverage and power, and it does not bound foreign CPU. Every one of those passes on the raw evidence: all 3606 pressure samples level 1, maximum gap 0.279919 s, Swapouts delta exactly zero in all twelve arms, Swapins delta sum +1288 with no resets and context only, 24 of 24 power observations AC with lowpowermode 0 and charge at or above the floor and each bracketing its arm, caffeinate in 371 of 371 samples. So my recommendation is unchanged: bounded acceptance, with the item 7 wording in place of any clean-host language.

9. REPORT BOUNDARY VERIFIED, INCLUDING THE BODY ARM. Your clarification is not just defensible, it is exactly what the data says, and it holds identically in all twelve arms with one distinct tuple per label. body: ParsedFiles 1, generation 1 to 2 so it does advance, owner_scope_count 0 so the frozen replacement scope is empty, messages_observed 2 and batches_observed 0 so Begin and End are published with zero fact batches, OwnersPublished 0, completeness_status success. So the body arm is source-changed and fact-unchanged and must not be described as exercising changed-fact payload delivery. structural: scope 1 owner, 3 messages, 1 batch, generation 2 to 3, 22 parsed. initial: scope 11284 owners, 3083 messages, 3081 batches, 7714 owners published, 6749 parsed, generation 0 to 1; that 3081 is the same batch count my payload-byte arithmetic used, which is why the +3084 resolves to the byte. noop carries no wire object at all, generation 1 to 1, zero parses, so genuinely silent is correct.
Other RESULTS.md figures I checked against the evidence: Swapins +1288 exact, Swapouts zero everywhere, 3606 pressure samples, maximum gap 0.279919 s, 110 packages with 99 cached and graphsession uncached at 512.044 s, delta parses 3/14/1453, the traced alias phase 73 to 16 ms, the run-identifier explanation of the payload bytes, and the outer prototype 042a0c6e superseded by 15f55895. All accurate as published.
Histories: all six steps across the three receipts have baseline cold hash equal to candidate cold hash equal to the effective hash, noop silent with zero parses and unchanged generation and zero wire messages, published true, gates present and all passing, problems empty, and all six series gates including both binary pins and the policy, observer, NATS, source-head and commit-chain pins pass. As an extra coherence check the endpoint hashes agree across receipts where commit endpoints overlap: history-source index 1 equals history-recent index 0, and history-recent index 1 equals history-broad index 1. Correctness only, no history performance claim, agreed.
One optional wording note. Line 20 says the independent review reproduced every criterion with no blockers, which is accurate, but a reader of that line alone could take it as clean-host endorsement; pairing it with the line 36 attribution caveat, or a five-word pointer to it, would close that. Your call, and not worth a republish on its own.

10. OVERLAY CANDIDATE. Noted as outside Stage37, not in checkout or main, and not affecting the reviewed source or evidence. I have not looked at it and will not unless you send a concrete review request.

Idle and source-only. Standing offer unchanged for the next cohort: gate-by-gate verification of the computed summary against the frozen text, including the conditions that pass, with no host access and no runs.
